   373→        writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   374→        ctx.log_sections.append(
   375→            f"{ctx.header}\n\nTIMEOUT after {deps.timeout_seconds}s\n{exc}\n"
   376→        )
   377→        ctx.safe_write_text_fn(ctx.log_file, "\n\n".join(ctx.log_sections))
   378→        return _ExecutionResult(code=124, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=124)
   379→    except OSError as exc:
   380→        state.stop_event.set()
   381→        writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   382→        ctx.log_sections.append(f"{ctx.header}\n\nRUNNER ERROR:\n{exc}\n")
   383→        ctx.safe_write_text_fn(ctx.log_file, "\n\n".join(ctx.log_sections))
   384→        return _ExecutionResult(code=127, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=127)
   385→    except (RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive boundary
   386→        state.stop_event.set()
   387→        writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   388→        ctx.log_sections.append(f"{ctx.header}\n\nUNEXPECTED RUNNER ERROR:\n{exc}\n")
   389→        ctx.safe_write_text_fn(ctx.log_file, "\n\n".join(ctx.log_sections))
   390→        return _ExecutionResult(code=1, stdout_text="", stderr_text="", early_return=1)
   391→    finally:
   392→        state.stop_event.set()
   393→        writer_thread.join(timeout=2)
   394→
   395→    return _ExecutionResult(
   396→        code=int(result.returncode),
   397→        stdout_text=result.stdout or "",
   398→        stderr_text=result.stderr or "",
   399→    )
   400→
   401→
   402→def run_codex_batch(
   403→    *,
   404→    prompt: str,
   405→    repo_root: Path,
   406→    output_file: Path,
   407→    log_file: Path,
   408→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   409→    codex_batch_command_fn=codex_batch_command,
   410→) -> int:
   411→    """Execute one codex batch and return a stable CLI-style status code."""
   412→    cmd = codex_batch_command_fn(
   413→        prompt=prompt,
   414→        repo_root=repo_root,
   415→        output_file=output_file,
   416→    )
   417→    retries_raw = deps.max_retries if isinstance(deps.max_retries, int) else 0
   418→    max_retries = max(0, retries_raw)
   419→    max_attempts = max_retries + 1
   420→    backoff_raw = (
   421→        float(deps.retry_backoff_seconds)
   422→        if isinstance(deps.retry_backoff_seconds, int | float)
   423→        else 0.0
   424→    )
   425→    retry_backoff_seconds = max(0.0, backoff_raw)
   426→    live_log_interval = (
   427→        float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds)
   428→        if isinstance(deps.live_log_interval_seconds, int | float)
   429→        and float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds) > 0
   430→        else 5.0
   431→    )
   432→    stall_seconds = (
   433→        int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds)
   434→        if isinstance(deps.stall_after_output_seconds, int | float)
   435→        and int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds) > 0
   436→        else 0
   437→    )
   438→    log_sections: list[str] = []
   439→    use_popen = bool(deps.use_popen_runner) and callable(
   440→        getattr(deps, "subprocess_popen", None)
   441→    )
   442→
   443→    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts + 1):
   444→        header = f"ATTEMPT {attempt}/{max_attempts}\n$ {' '.join(cmd)}"
   445→        started_monotonic = time.monotonic()
   446→        state = _RunnerState(last_stream_activity=started_monotonic)
   447→        ctx = _AttemptContext(
   448→            header=header,
   449→            started_at_iso=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   450→            started_monotonic=started_monotonic,
   451→            output_file=output_file,
   452→            log_file=log_file,
   453→            log_sections=log_sections,
   454→            safe_write_text_fn=deps.safe_write_text_fn,
   455→        )
   456→        _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   457→
   458→        if use_popen:
   459→            result = _run_via_popen(
   460→                cmd,
   461→                deps,
   462→                state,
   463→                ctx,
   464→                live_log_interval,
   465→                stall_seconds,
   466→            )
   467→        else:
   468→            result = _run_via_subprocess(cmd, deps, state, ctx, live_log_interval)
   469→
   470→        if result.early_return is not None:
   471→            return result.early_return
   472→
   473→        if result.timed_out:
   474→            log_sections.append(
   475→                f"{header}\n\nTIMEOUT after {deps.timeout_seconds}s\n\n"
   476→                f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   477→            )
   478→            if _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   479→                log_sections.append(
   480→                    "Recovered timed-out batch from JSON output file; "
   481→                    "continuing as success."
   482→                )
   483→                deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   484→                return 0
   485→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   486→            return 124
   487→
   488→        if result.stalled:
   489→            log_sections.append(
   490→                f"{header}\n\nSTALL RECOVERY after {stall_seconds}s "
   491→                "of stable output and no stream activity.\n\n"
   492→                f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   493→            )
   494→            if _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   495→                log_sections.append(
   496→                    "Recovered stalled batch from JSON output file; "
   497→                    "continuing as success."
   498→                )
   499→                deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   500→                return 0
   501→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   502→            return 124
   503→
   504→        log_sections.append(
   505→            f"{header}\n\nSTDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   506→        )
   507→
   508→        if result.code == 0:
   509→            if not _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   510→                log_sections.append(
   511→                    "Runner exited 0 but output file is missing or invalid; "
   512→                    "treating as execution failure."
   513→                )
   514→                deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   515→                return 1
   516→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   517→            return 0
   518→
   519→        combined = f"{result.stdout_text}\n{result.stderr_text}".lower()
   520→        is_transient = any(needle in combined for needle in _TRANSIENT_RUNNER_PHRASES)
   521→        if not is_transient or attempt >= max_attempts:
   522→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   523→            return result.code
   524→
   525→        delay_seconds = retry_backoff_seconds * (2 ** (attempt - 1))
   526→        log_sections.append(
   527→            "Transient runner failure detected; "
   528→            f"retrying in {delay_seconds:.1f}s (attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_attempts})."
   529→        )
   530→        try:
   531→            if delay_seconds > 0:
   532→                deps.sleep_fn(delay_seconds)
   533→        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
   534→            log_sections.append(
   535→                f"Retry delay hook failed: {exc} — aborting remaining retries."
   536→            )
   537→            deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   538→            return 1
   539→
   540→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   541→    return 1
   542→
   543→
   544→def run_followup_scan(
   545→    *,
   546→    lang_name: str,
   547→    scan_path: str,
   548→    deps: FollowupScanDeps,
   549→) -> int:
   550→    """Run a follow-up scan and return a non-zero status when it fails."""
   551→    scan_cmd = [
   552→        deps.python_executable,
   553→        "-m",
   554→        "desloppify",
   555→        "--lang",
   556→        lang_name,
   557→        "scan",
   558→        "--path",
   559→        scan_path,
   560→    ]
   561→    print(deps.colorize_fn("\n  Running follow-up scan...", "bold"))
   562→    try:
   563→        result = deps.subprocess_run(
   564→            scan_cmd,
   565→            cwd=str(deps.project_root),
   566→            timeout=deps.timeout_seconds,
   567→        )
   568→    except deps.timeout_error:
   569→        print(
   570→            deps.colorize_fn(
   571→                f"  Follow-up scan timed out after {deps.timeout_seconds}s.",
   572→                "yellow",
   573→            ),
   574→            file=sys.stderr,
   575→        )
   576→        return 124
   577→    except OSError as exc:
   578→        print(
   579→            deps.colorize_fn(f"  Follow-up scan failed: {exc}", "red"),
   580→            file=sys.stderr,
   581→        )
   582→        return 1
   583→    return int(getattr(result, "returncode", 0) or 0)
   584→
   585→
   586→__all__ = [
   587→    "CodexBatchRunnerDeps",
   588→    "FollowupScanDeps",
   589→    "codex_batch_command",
   590→    "run_codex_batch",
   591→    "run_followup_scan",
   592→]
   593→

   187→def _compute_abstraction_components(
   188→    merged_assessments: dict[str, float],
   189→    abstraction_axis_scores: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]],
   190→    *,
   191→    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
   192→    abstraction_component_names: dict[str, str],
   193→) -> dict[str, float] | None:
   194→    abstraction_score = merged_assessments.get("abstraction_fitness")
   195→    if abstraction_score is None:
   196→        return None
   197→
   198→    component_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
   199→    for axis in abstraction_sub_axes:
   200→        weighted = abstraction_axis_scores.get(axis, [])
   201→        if not weighted:
   202→            continue
   203→        numerator = sum(score * weight for score, weight in weighted)
   204→        denominator = sum(weight for _, weight in weighted)
   205→        if denominator <= 0:
   206→            continue
   207→        component_scores[abstraction_component_names[axis]] = round(
   208→            max(0.0, min(100.0, numerator / denominator)),
   209→            1,
   210→        )
   211→    return component_scores if component_scores else None
   212→
   213→
   214→def merge_batch_results(
   215→    batch_results: list[dict[str, Any]],
   216→    *,
   217→    abstraction_sub_axes: tuple[str, ...],
   218→    abstraction_component_names: dict[str, str],
   219→) -> dict[str, object]:
   220→    """Deterministically merge assessments/findings across batch outputs."""
   221→    score_buckets: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = {}
   222→    score_raw_by_dim: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
   223→    finding_map: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   224→    merged_dimension_notes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   225→    coverage_values: list[float] = []
   226→    evidence_density_values: list[float] = []
   227→    high_score_missing_issue_note_total = 0.0
   228→    abstraction_axis_scores: dict[str, list[tuple[float, float]]] = {
   229→        axis: [] for axis in abstraction_sub_axes
   230→    }
   231→
   232→    for result in batch_results:
   233→        _accumulate_batch_scores(
   234→            result,
   235→            score_buckets=score_buckets,
   236→            score_raw_by_dim=score_raw_by_dim,
   237→            merged_dimension_notes=merged_dimension_notes,
   238→            abstraction_axis_scores=abstraction_axis_scores,
   239→            abstraction_sub_axes=abstraction_sub_axes,
   240→        )
   241→        _accumulate_batch_findings(result, finding_map)
   242→        high_score_missing_issue_note_total += _accumulate_batch_quality(
   243→            result,
   244→            coverage_values=coverage_values,
   245→            evidence_density_values=evidence_density_values,
   246→        )
   247→
   248→    merged_findings = list(finding_map.values())
   249→    finding_pressure_by_dim, finding_count_by_dim = _finding_pressure_by_dimension(
   250→        merged_findings,
   251→        dimension_notes=merged_dimension_notes,
   252→    )
   253→
   254→    merged_assessments = _compute_merged_assessments(
   255→        score_buckets, score_raw_by_dim, finding_pressure_by_dim, finding_count_by_dim
   256→    )
   257→
   258→    merged_assessment_payload: dict[str, float | dict[str, object]] = {
   259→        key: value for key, value in merged_assessments.items()
   260→    }
   261→    component_scores = _compute_abstraction_components(
   262→        merged_assessments,
   263→        abstraction_axis_scores,
   264→        abstraction_sub_axes=abstraction_sub_axes,
   265→        abstraction_component_names=abstraction_component_names,
   266→    )
   267→    if component_scores is not None:
   268→        merged_assessment_payload["abstraction_fitness"] = {
   269→            "score": merged_assessments["abstraction_fitness"],
   270→            "components": list(component_scores),
   271→            "component_scores": component_scores,
   272→        }
   273→
   274→    return {
   275→        "assessments": merged_assessment_payload,
   276→        "dimension_notes": merged_dimension_notes,
   277→        "findings": merged_findings,
   278→        "review_quality": {
   279→            "batch_count": len(batch_results),
   280→            "dimension_coverage": round(
   281→                sum(coverage_values) / max(len(coverage_values), 1),
   282→                3,
   283→            ),
   284→            "evidence_density": round(
   285→                sum(evidence_density_values) / max(len(evidence_density_values), 1),
   286→                3,
   287→            ),
   288→            REVIEW_QUALITY_HIGH_SCORE_MISSING_ISSUES_KEY: int(
   289→                high_score_missing_issue_note_total
   290→            ),
   291→            "finding_pressure": round(sum(finding_pressure_by_dim.values()), 3),
   292→            "dimensions_with_findings": len(finding_count_by_dim),
   293→        },
   294→    }
   295→
   296→
   297→__all__ = ["assessment_weight", "merge_batch_results"]
   298→

   154→    def _report_heartbeat(self, details: dict[str, object]) -> None:

   248→def resolve_run_log_path(
   249→    raw_run_log_file: object,
   250→    *,
   251→    project_root: Path,
   252→    run_dir: Path,
   253→) -> Path:
   254→    if isinstance(raw_run_log_file, str) and raw_run_log_file.strip():
   255→        candidate = Path(raw_run_log_file.strip()).expanduser()
   256→        run_log_path = candidate if candidate.is_absolute() else project_root / candidate
   257→    else:
   258→        run_log_path = run_dir / "run.log"
   259→    run_log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   260→    return run_log_path
   261→
   262→
   263→def make_run_log_writer(run_log_path: Path) -> Callable[[str], None]:
   264→    def _append_run_log(message: str) -> None:
   265→        line = f"{datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec='seconds')} {message}\n"
   266→        try:
   267→            with run_log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   268→                handle.write(line)
   269→        except OSError:
   270→            return
   271→
   272→    return _append_run_log

   319→        "allow_partial": summary_config.allow_partial,
   320→        "max_parallel_batches": (

   322→        ),

   324→        "batch_max_retries": summary_config.batch_max_retries,
   325→        "batch_retry_backoff_seconds": summary_config.batch_retry_backoff_seconds,
   326→        "batch_heartbeat_seconds": (

   328→        ),

   331→        ),

   333→        "immutable_packet": str(summary_config.immutable_packet_path),

    91→def collect_reviewed_files_from_batches(

    94→    selected_indexes: list[int],
    95→) -> list[str]:
    96→    """Collect normalized file paths reviewed in the selected batch set."""
    97→    reviewed: list[str] = []

    99→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   100→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(batches):

   102→        batch = batches[idx]

   111→                continue
   112→            if path.endswith("/"):

   114→            if path in seen:

   116→            seen.add(path)
   117→            reviewed.append(path)

   561→+def _lang_from_scan_history(state: dict) -> str | None:
   562→+    history = state.get("scan_history")
   563→+    if not isinstance(history, list):
   564→+        return None
   565→+    for entry in reversed(history):
   566→+        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   567→+            continue
   568→+        lang = entry.get("lang")
   569→+        if isinstance(lang, str) and lang.strip():
   570→+            return lang.strip().lower()
   571→+    return None
   572→+
   573→+
   574→+def _lang_from_capabilities(state: dict) -> str | None:
   575→+    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
   576→+    if not isinstance(capabilities, dict) or len(capabilities) != 1:
   577→+        return None
   578→+    only_lang = next(iter(capabilities.keys()))
   579→+    if isinstance(only_lang, str) and only_lang.strip():
   580→+        return only_lang.strip().lower()
   581→+    return None
   582→+
   583→+
   584→+def _lang_from_findings(state: dict) -> str | None:
   585→+    findings = state.get("findings")
   586→+    if not isinstance(findings, dict):
   587→+        return None
   588→+    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   589→+    for finding in findings.values():
   590→+        if not isinstance(finding, dict):
   591→+            continue
   592→+        lang = finding.get("lang")
   593→+        if not isinstance(lang, str) or not lang.strip():
   594→+            continue
   595→+        key = lang.strip().lower()
   596→+        counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
   597→+    if counts:
   598→+        return max(counts, key=counts.get)
   599→+    return None
   600→+
   601→+
   602→+def resolve_scorecard_lang(state: dict) -> str | None:
   603→+    """Best-effort current scan language key for scorecard display policy."""
   604→+    return (
   605→+        _lang_from_scan_history(state)
   606→+        or _lang_from_capabilities(state)
   607→+        or _lang_from_findings(state)
   608→+    )
   609→+
   610→+
   611→+def is_unassessed_subjective_placeholder(data: dict) -> bool:
   612→+    return (
   613→+        "subjective_assessment" in data.get("detectors", {})
   614→+        and data.get("score", 0) == 0
   615→+        and data.get("issues", 0) == 0
   616→+    )
   617→+
   618→+
   619→+def collapse_elegance_dimensions(
   620→+    active_dims: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   621→+    *,
   622→+    lang_key: str | None,
   623→+) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
   624→+    """Collapse High/Mid/Low elegance rows into one aggregate display row."""
   625→+    component_names = set(
   626→+        _ELEGANCE_COMPONENTS_BY_LANG.get(lang_key or "", _DEFAULT_ELEGANCE_COMPONENTS)
   627→+    )
   628→+    elegance_rows = [
   629→+        (name, data) for name, data in active_dims if name in component_names
   630→+    ]
   631→+    if not elegance_rows:
   632→+        return active_dims
   633→+
   634→+    remaining_rows = [
   635→+        (name, data) for name, data in active_dims if name not in component_names
   636→+    ]
   637→+    count = len(elegance_rows)
   638→+    score_avg = round(
   639→+        sum(float(data.get("score", 100.0)) for _, data in elegance_rows) / count, 1
   640→+    )
   641→+    strict_avg = round(
   642→+        sum(
   643→+            float(data.get("strict", data.get("score", 100.0)))
   644→+            for _, data in elegance_rows
   645→+        )
   646→+        / count,
   647→+        1,
   648→+    )
   649→+    checks_total = sum(int(data.get("checks", 0)) for _, data in elegance_rows)
   650→+    issues_total = sum(int(data.get("issues", 0)) for _, data in elegance_rows)
   651→+    tier = max(int(data.get("tier", 4)) for _, data in elegance_rows)
   652→+    placeholder_flags = [
   653→+        bool(
   654→+            data.get("detectors", {})
   655→+            .get("subjective_assessment", {})
   656→+            .get("placeholder")
   657→+        )
   658→+        for _, data in elegance_rows
   659→+    ]
   660→+
   661→+    label = "Elegance"
   662→+    if any(name.lower() == label.lower() for name, _ in remaining_rows):
   663→+        label = "Elegance (combined)"
   664→+
   665→+    pass_rate = round(score_avg / 100.0, 4)
   666→+    return [
   667→+        *remaining_rows,
   668→+        (
   669→+            label,
   670→+            {
   671→+                "score": score_avg,
   672→+                "strict": strict_avg,
   673→+                "checks": checks_total,
   674→+                "issues": issues_total,
   675→+                "tier": tier,
   676→+                "detectors": {
   677→+                    "subjective_assessment": {
   678→+                        "potential": checks_total,
   679→+                        "pass_rate": pass_rate,
   680→+                        "issues": issues_total,
   681→+                        "weighted_failures": round(checks_total * (1 - pass_rate), 4),
   682→+                        "components": [name for name, _ in elegance_rows],
   683→+                        "placeholder": any(placeholder_flags),
   684→+                    }
   685→+                },
   686→+            },
   687→+        ),
   688→+    ]
   689→+

   691→+def limit_scorecard_dimensions(
   692→+    active_dims: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   693→+    *,
   694→+    lang_key: str | None,
   695→+    max_rows: int = _SCORECARD_MAX_DIMENSIONS,
   696→+) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
   697→+    """Limit scorecard rows with language-specific subjective priority."""
   698→+    if len(active_dims) <= max_rows:
   699→+        return active_dims
   700→+
   701→+    mechanical = [
   702→+        (name, data)
   703→+        for name, data in active_dims
   704→+        if "subjective_assessment" not in data.get("detectors", {})
   705→+    ]
   706→+    subjective = [
   707→+        (name, data)
   708→+        for name, data in active_dims
   709→+        if "subjective_assessment" in data.get("detectors", {})
   710→+    ]
   711→+    if len(mechanical) >= max_rows:
   712→+        return mechanical[:max_rows]
   713→+
   714→+    budget = max_rows - len(mechanical)
   715→+    preferred_order = _SUBJECTIVE_SCORECARD_ORDER_BY_LANG.get(
   716→+        lang_key or "",
   717→+        _SUBJECTIVE_SCORECARD_ORDER_DEFAULT,
   718→+    )
   719→+
   720→+    remaining = {name: (name, data) for name, data in subjective}
   721→+    selected: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
   722→+    for name in preferred_order:
   723→+        row = remaining.pop(name, None)
   724→+        if row is None:
   725→+            continue
   726→+        selected.append(row)
   727→+        if len(selected) >= budget:
   728→+            break
   729→+
   730→+    if len(selected) < budget and remaining:
   731→+        extras = sorted(
   732→+            remaining.values(),
   733→+            key=lambda item: (
   734→+                float(item[1].get("strict", item[1].get("score", 100.0))),
   735→+                item[0],
   736→+            ),
   737→+        )
   738→+        selected.extend(extras[: budget - len(selected)])
   739→+
   740→+    return [*mechanical, *selected]
   741→+
   742→+
   743→+def prepare_scorecard_dimensions(state: dict) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
   744→+    """Prepare scorecard rows (active, elegance-collapsed, capped)."""
   745→+    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   746→+    if not isinstance(dim_scores, dict):

   748→+
   749→+    all_dims = [
   750→+        (name, data) for name, data in dim_scores.items() if isinstance(data, dict)
   751→+    ]
   752→+
   753→+    [REDACTED](state)
   754→+    all_dims = collapse_elegance_dimensions(all_dims, lang_key=lang_key)
   755→+
   756→+    active_dims = [
   757→+        (name, data)
   758→+        for name, data in all_dims
   759→+        if data.get("checks", 0) > 0 and not is_unassessed_subjective_placeholder(data)

+def _lang_from_scan_history(state: dict) -> str | None:
+    history = state.get("scan_history")
+    if not isinstance(history, list):
+        return None
+    for entry in reversed(history):
+        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
+            continue
+        lang = entry.get("lang")
+        if isinstance(lang, str) and lang.strip():
+            return lang.strip().lower()
+    return None
+
+
+def _lang_from_capabilities(state: dict) -> str | None:
+    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
+    if not isinstance(capabilities, dict) or len(capabilities) != 1:
+        return None
+    only_lang = next(iter(capabilities.keys()))
+    if isinstance(only_lang, str) and only_lang.strip():
+        return only_lang.strip().lower()
+    return None
+
+
+def _lang_from_findings(state: dict) -> str | None:
+    findings = state.get("findings")
+    if not isinstance(findings, dict):
+        return None
+    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
+    for finding in findings.values():
+        if not isinstance(finding, dict):
+            continue
+        lang = finding.get("lang")
+        if not isinstance(lang, str) or not lang.strip():
+            continue
+        key = lang.strip().lower()
+        counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
+    if counts:
+        return max(counts, key=counts.get)
+    return None
+
+
+def resolve_scorecard_lang(state: dict) -> str | None:
+    """Best-effort current scan language key for scorecard display policy."""
+    return (
+        _lang_from_scan_history(state)
+        or _lang_from_capabilities(state)
+        or _lang_from_findings(state)
+    )
+

+    return (

+        and data.get("score", 0) == 0

+def collapse_elegance_dimensions(
+    active_dims: list[tuple[str, dict]],

+) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
+    """Collapse High/Mid/Low elegance rows into one aggregate display row."""
+    component_names = set(

+    )
+    elegance_rows = [
+        (name, data) for name, data in active_dims if name in component_names
+    ]
+    if not elegance_rows:
+        return active_dims
+
+    remaining_rows = [
+        (name, data) for name, data in active_dims if name not in component_names
+    ]
+    count = len(elegance_rows)
+    score_avg = round(
+        sum(float(data.get("score", 100.0)) for _, data in elegance_rows) / count, 1
+    )
+    strict_avg = round(
+        sum(
+            float(data.get("strict", data.get("score", 100.0)))
+            for _, data in elegance_rows
+        )
+        / count,
+        1,
+    )
+    checks_total = sum(int(data.get("checks", 0)) for _, data in elegance_rows)
+    issues_total = sum(int(data.get("issues", 0)) for _, data in elegance_rows)
+    tier = max(int(data.get("tier", 4)) for _, data in elegance_rows)

   124→    return runner_packets_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(
   125→        runner=runner,
   126→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   127→        run_stamp=run_stamp,
   128→        batch_indexes=batch_indexes,
   129→    )
   130→
   131→
   132→def selected_batch_indexes(
   133→    *,
   134→    raw_selection: str | None,
   135→    batch_count: int,
   136→    parse_fn,
   137→    colorize_fn,
   138→) -> list[int]:

   143→        parse_fn=parse_fn,

   145→    )
   146→
   147→
   148→def prepare_run_artifacts(
   149→    *,
   150→    stamp: str,
   151→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   152→    batches: list[dict],
   153→    packet_path: Path,
   154→    run_root: Path,
   155→    repo_root: Path,
   156→    build_prompt_fn,
   157→    safe_write_text_fn,
   158→    colorize_fn,
   159→) -> tuple[Path, Path, dict[int, Path], dict[int, Path], dict[int, Path]]:
   160→    """Build prompt/output/log paths and persist prompts for selected batches."""
   161→    return runner_packets_mod.prepare_run_artifacts(
   162→        stamp=stamp,
   163→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   164→        batches=batches,
   165→        packet_path=packet_path,
   166→        run_root=run_root,
   167→        repo_root=repo_root,
   168→        build_prompt_fn=build_prompt_fn,
   169→        safe_write_text_fn=safe_write_text_fn,
   170→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   171→    )
   172→
   173→
   174→def execute_batches(
   175→    *,
   176→    tasks: dict[int, object],
   177→    run_parallel: bool,
   178→    progress_fn=None,
   179→    error_log_fn=None,
   180→    max_parallel_workers: int | None = None,
   181→    heartbeat_seconds: float | None = 15.0,
   182→    clock_fn=time.monotonic,
   183→) -> list[int]:
   184→    """Run indexed tasks and return failed index list."""
   185→    return runner_parallel_mod.execute_batches(
   186→        tasks=tasks,
   187→        run_parallel=run_parallel,
   188→        progress_fn=progress_fn,
   189→        error_log_fn=error_log_fn,
   190→        max_parallel_workers=max_parallel_workers,
   191→        heartbeat_seconds=heartbeat_seconds,
   192→        clock_fn=clock_fn,
   193→    )
   194→
   195→
   196→def _extract_payload_from_log(
   197→    batch_index: int,
   198→    raw_path: Path,
   199→    extract_fn,
   200→) -> dict[str, object] | None:
   201→    """Try to recover a batch payload from the runner log file."""
   202→    log_path = raw_path.parent.parent / "logs" / f"batch-{batch_index + 1}.log"
   203→    if not log_path.exists():
   204→        return None
   205→    try:
   206→        log_text = log_path.read_text()
   207→    except OSError:
   208→        return None
   209→
   210→    stdout_marker = "\nSTDOUT:\n"
   211→    stderr_marker = "\n\nSTDERR:\n"
   212→    stdout_start = log_text.rfind(stdout_marker)
   213→    if stdout_start == -1 and log_text.startswith("STDOUT:\n"):
   214→        stdout_start = 0
   215→        stdout_offset = len("STDOUT:\n")
   216→    elif stdout_start >= 0:
   217→        stdout_offset = len(stdout_marker)
   218→    else:
   219→        stdout_offset = 0
   220→    if stdout_start >= 0:
   221→        start_idx = stdout_start + stdout_offset
   222→        stdout_end = log_text.find(stderr_marker, start_idx)
   223→        stdout_text = (
   224→            log_text[start_idx:]
   225→            if stdout_end == -1
   226→            else log_text[start_idx:stdout_end]
   227→        )
   228→        payload = extract_fn(stdout_text)
   229→        if payload is not None:
   230→            return payload
   231→        return None
   232→
   233→    return extract_fn(log_text)
   234→
   235→
   236→def collect_batch_results(
   237→    *,
   238→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   239→    failures: list[int],
   240→    output_files: dict[int, Path],
   241→    allowed_dims: set[str],
   242→    extract_payload_fn,
   243→    normalize_result_fn,
   244→) -> tuple[list[BatchResult], list[int]]:
   245→    """Parse and normalize batch outputs, preserving prior failures."""
   246→    batch_results: list[BatchResult] = []
   247→    failure_set = set(failures)
   248→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   249→        had_execution_failure = idx in failure_set
   250→        raw_path = output_files[idx]
   251→        payload = None
   252→        parsed_from_log = False
   253→        if raw_path.exists():
   254→            try:
   255→                payload = extract_payload_fn(raw_path.read_text())
   256→            except OSError:
   257→                payload = None
   258→        if payload is None:
   259→            payload = _extract_payload_from_log(idx, raw_path, extract_payload_fn)
   260→            parsed_from_log = payload is not None
   261→        if payload is None:
   262→            failure_set.add(idx)
   263→            continue
   264→        if parsed_from_log:
   265→            try:
   266→                raw_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   267→            except OSError as exc:
   268→                logger.debug("Failed to write recovered payload to raw file: %s", exc)
   269→        try:
   270→            assessments, findings, dimension_notes, quality = normalize_result_fn(
   271→                payload,
   272→                allowed_dims,
   273→            )
   274→        except ValueError:
   275→            failure_set.add(idx)
   276→            continue
   277→        if had_execution_failure:
   278→            failure_set.discard(idx)
   279→        batch_results.append(
   280→            BatchResult(
   281→                batch_index=idx + 1,
   282→                assessments=assessments,
   283→                dimension_notes=dimension_notes,
   284→                findings=findings,
   285→                quality=quality,
   286→            )
   287→        )
   288→    return batch_results, sorted(failure_set)
   289→
   290→

   292→    "BatchProgressEvent",

"""Shared subjective-dimension metadata used by scoring and review layers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from functools import lru_cache

from desloppify.core._internal.text_utils import is_numeric

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DISPLAY_NAMES: dict[str, str] = {
    # Holistic dimensions
    "cross_module_architecture": "Cross-module arch",
    "initialization_coupling": "Init coupling",
    "convention_outlier": "Convention drift",
    "error_consistency": "Error consistency",
    "abstraction_fitness": "Abstraction fit",
    "dependency_health": "Dep health",
    "test_strategy": "Test strategy",
    "api_surface_coherence": "API coherence",
    "authorization_consistency": "Auth consistency",
    "ai_generated_debt": "AI generated debt",
    "incomplete_migration": "Stale migration",
    "package_organization": "Structure nav",
    "high_level_elegance": "High elegance",
    "mid_level_elegance": "Mid elegance",
    "low_level_elegance": "Low elegance",
    # Design coherence (concerns bridge)
    "design_coherence": "Design coherence",
    # Per-file review dimensions
    "naming_quality": "Naming quality",
    "logic_clarity": "Logic clarity",
    "type_safety": "Type safety",
    "contract_coherence": "Contracts",
}

_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES: dict[str, str] = DISPLAY_NAMES

_LEGACY_SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHTS_BY_DISPLAY: dict[str, float] = {
    "high elegance": 22.0,
    "mid elegance": 22.0,
    "low elegance": 12.0,
    "contracts": 12.0,
    "type safety": 12.0,
    "abstraction fit": 8.0,
    "logic clarity": 6.0,
    "structure nav": 5.0,
    "error consistency": 3.0,
    "naming quality": 2.0,
    "ai generated debt": 1.0,
}

_LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        "naming_quality",
        "error_consistency",
        "abstraction_fitness",
        "logic_clarity",
        "ai_generated_debt",
        "type_safety",
        "contract_coherence",
        "package_organization",
        "high_level_elegance",
        "mid_level_elegance",
        "low_level_elegance",
    }
)

_LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION: dict[str, float] = {}
for _dimension_key, _display_name in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
    _weight = _LEGACY_SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHTS_BY_DISPLAY.get(
        " ".join(_display_name.strip().lower().split())
    )
    if _weight is not None:
        _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION[_dimension_key] = _weight


def _normalize_dimension_name(name: str) -> str:
    return "_".join(str(name).strip().lower().replace("-", "_").split())


def _title_display_name(dimension_key: str) -> str:
    return dimension_key.replace("_", " ").title()


def _normalize_lang_name(lang_name: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not isinstance(lang_name, str):
        return None
    cleaned = lang_name.strip().lower()
    return cleaned or None


def _extract_prompt_meta(entry: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        return {}
    meta = entry.get("meta")
    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
        return {}
    out: dict[str, object] = {}

    if isinstance(meta.get("display_name"), str) and meta["display_name"].strip():
        out["display_name"] = meta["display_name"].strip()

    weight = meta.get("weight")
    if is_numeric(weight):
        out["weight"] = max(0.0, float(weight))

    enabled = meta.get("enabled_by_default")
    if isinstance(enabled, bool):
        out["enabled_by_default"] = enabled

    reset_on_scan = meta.get("reset_on_scan")
    if isinstance(reset_on_scan, bool):
        out["reset_on_scan"] = reset_on_scan

    return out


def _merge_dimension_meta(
    target: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
    *,
    dimensions: list[str],
    prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
    override_existing: bool = False,
) -> None:
    defaults = {
        _normalize_dimension_name(dim)
        for dim in dimensions
        if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
    }

    for raw_dim, entry in prompts.items():
        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw_dim)
        if not dim:
            continue

        payload = target.setdefault(dim, {})
        prompt_meta = _extract_prompt_meta(entry)

        if "display_name" in prompt_meta and (
            override_existing or "display_name" not in payload
        ):
            payload["display_name"] = prompt_meta["display_name"]
        if "weight" in prompt_meta and (override_existing or "weight" not in payload):
            payload["weight"] = prompt_meta["weight"]
        if "reset_on_scan" in prompt_meta and (
            override_existing or "reset_on_scan" not in payload
        ):
            payload["reset_on_scan"] = prompt_meta["reset_on_scan"]

        if dim in defaults:
            payload["enabled_by_default"] = True
        if "enabled_by_default" in prompt_meta:
            if override_existing:
                payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"])
            else:
                payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(
                    payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)
                    or prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"]
                )


def _available_languages() -> list[str]:
    try:
        from desloppify.languages import available_langs

        return list(available_langs())
    except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError):
        return []


def _load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
    from desloppify.intelligence.review.dimensions.data import load_dimensions

    return load_dimensions()


def _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
    lang_name: str,
) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
    from desloppify.intelligence.review.dimensions.data import load_dimensions_for_lang

    return load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)


def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    normalized: list[str] = []
    for raw in values:
        if not isinstance(raw, str):
            continue
        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
        if not dim or dim in normalized:
            continue
        normalized.append(dim)
    return tuple(normalized)


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
    try:
        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)


@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
    if normalized is None:
        return default_dimension_keys()
    try:
        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        logger.debug(
            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
            normalized,
            exc,
        )
        return default_dimension_keys()
    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)


def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
    *,
    lang_name: str | None,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}

    try:
        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)

    langs = (
        [lang_name]
        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
        else _available_languages()
    )
    for name in langs:
        try:
            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
            _merge_dimension_meta(
                out,
                dimensions=lang_defaults,
                prompts=lang_prompts,
                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
            )
        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
            continue

    for dim, payload in out.items():
        payload.setdefault(
            "display_name",
            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
        )
        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
        else:
            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)

    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)

    return out


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)


@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
    lang_name: str | None,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)


def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
    if normalized is None:
        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)


def get_dimension_metadata(
    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))

    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
    return payload


def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))


def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
    if is_numeric(raw):
        return max(0.0, float(raw))
    return 1.0


def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
            continue
        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
    return out


def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
    out = []
    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
            continue
        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
            continue
        out.append(dim)
    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))


__all__ = [
    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
    "default_dimension_keys",
    "default_dimension_keys_for_lang",
    "default_display_names_map",
    "dimension_display_name",
    "dimension_weight",
    "get_dimension_metadata",
    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata",
    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang",
    "resettable_default_dimensions",
]

}
_MECHANICAL_SCORECARD_DIMENSIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "File health",
    "Code quality",
    "Duplication",
    "Test health",
    "Security",
)


def _compose_scorecard_dimensions(subjective_order: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    merged: list[str] = []
    for name in (*_MECHANICAL_SCORECARD_DIMENSIONS, *subjective_order):
        if name not in merged:
            merged.append(name)
    return tuple(merged[:_SCORECARD_MAX_DIMENSIONS])


_SCORECARD_DIMENSIONS_BY_LANG: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "python": _compose_scorecard_dimensions(_SUBJECTIVE_SCORECARD_ORDER_BY_LANG["python"]),
    "typescript": _compose_scorecard_dimensions(_SUBJECTIVE_SCORECARD_ORDER_BY_LANG["typescript"]),
    "csharp": _compose_scorecard_dimensions(_SUBJECTIVE_SCORECARD_ORDER_BY_LANG["csharp"]),
}

"""Registry for optional language hook modules consumed by detectors."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import logging
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

_LANG_HOOKS: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = defaultdict(dict)
_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def register_lang_hooks(
    lang_name: str,
    *,
    test_coverage: object | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Register optional detector hook modules for a language."""
    hooks = _LANG_HOOKS[lang_name]
    if test_coverage is not None:
        hooks["test_coverage"] = test_coverage


def get_lang_hook(lang_name: str | None, hook_name: str) -> object | None:
    """Get a previously-registered language hook module."""
    if not lang_name:
        return None

    hook = _LANG_HOOKS.get(lang_name, {}).get(hook_name)
    if hook is not None:
        return hook

    module_name = f"desloppify.languages.{lang_name}"
    module = sys.modules.get(module_name)

    # Lazy-load only the requested language package.
    if module is None:
        try:
            importlib.import_module(module_name)
        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError, OSError) as exc:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "Unable to import language hook package %s: %s", lang_name, exc
            )
            return None
    elif lang_name not in _LANG_HOOKS:
        try:
            importlib.reload(module)
        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError, OSError) as exc:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "Unable to reload language hook package %s: %s", lang_name, exc
            )
            return None

    return _LANG_HOOKS.get(lang_name, {}).get(hook_name)


def clear_lang_hooks_for_tests() -> None:
    """Clear registry (test helper)."""
    _LANG_HOOKS.clear()


__all__ = [
    "clear_lang_hooks_for_tests",
    "get_lang_hook",
    "register_lang_hooks",
]

     2→

     7→
     8→_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]

    10→_ALLOWED_COMPAT_MODULES = {
    11→    "desloppify/utils.py",
    12→    "desloppify/file_discovery.py",
    13→}
    14→
    15→
    16→def _runtime_python_files() -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    17→    files: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    18→    for path in _PACKAGE_ROOT.rglob("*.py"):
    19→        rel = path.relative_to(_PROJECT_ROOT).as_posix()
    20→        if "/tests/" in rel:
    21→            continue
    22→        if rel in _ALLOWED_COMPAT_MODULES:
    23→            continue
    24→        files.append((path, rel))
    25→    return files
    26→
    27→
    28→def _compat_import_violations(path: Path, rel: str) -> list[str]:
    29→    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(), filename=str(path))
    30→    violations: list[str] = []
    31→
    32→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    33→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    34→            for alias in node.names:
    35→                if alias.name in {"desloppify.utils", "desloppify.file_discovery"}:
    36→                    violations.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} import {alias.name}")
    37→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
    38→            module = node.module or ""
    39→            if module in {"desloppify.utils", "desloppify.file_discovery"}:
    40→                violations.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} from {module} import ...")
    41→                continue
    42→            if module == "desloppify":
    43→                for alias in node.names:
    44→                    if alias.name in {"utils", "file_discovery"}:
    45→                        violations.append(
    46→                            f"{rel}:{node.lineno} from desloppify import {alias.name}"
    47→                        )
    48→    return violations
    49→
    50→
    51→def test_runtime_code_avoids_deprecated_compat_facades():
    52→    violations: list[str] = []
    53→    for path, rel in _runtime_python_files():
    54→        violations.extend(_compat_import_violations(path, rel))
    55→    assert not violations, "runtime imports deprecated compat facades:\n" + "\n".join(
    56→        sorted(violations)

+    def __fspath__(self) -> str:

+        except (TypeError, ValueError):

## Candid Assessment: Review Module Refactoring

### 1. `runner_helpers.py` (1512 lines -> 310 lines)

**Where did the code go?** It was extracted into four new modules, and `runner_helpers.py` was left as a thin re-export facade:

| New file | Lines | Content extracted from `runner_helpers.py` |
|---|---|---|
| `runner_failures.py` (324 lines) | Failure classification, hint generation, retry guidance printing (`classify_runner_failure`, `runner_failure_hints`, `print_failures`, `print_failures_and_exit`, etc.) |
| `runner_packets.py` (192 lines) | Packet sanitization, blind-packet construction, SHA hashing, artifact layout (`write_packet_snapshot`, `build_blind_packet`, `sha256_file`, `build_batch_import_provenance`, `selected_batch_indexes`, `prepare_run_artifacts`) |
| `runner_parallel.py` (353 lines) | Thread-pool execution, serial/parallel dispatch, heartbeat monitoring (`execute_batches`, `BatchProgressEvent`) |
| `runner_process.py` (592 lines) | Subprocess runner (Popen and subprocess.run paths), stall detection, retry logic, followup scan (`CodexBatchRunnerDeps`, `FollowupScanDeps`, `run_codex_batch`, `run_followup_scan`, `codex_batch_command`) |

**Total new: 1,461 lines.** The remaining 310 lines in `runner_helpers.py` are a compatibility shim that re-exports every public symbol from the new sub-modules plus the `BatchResult` dataclass and `collect_batch_results` logic (which stayed).

**Verdict:** This is a genuine extraction. No functionality was deleted. The original `runner_helpers.py` is now a backwards-compatible facade -- all existing imports (`from desloppify.app.commands.review import runner_helpers as runner_helpers_mod`) continue to work because every public name is re-exported. The test files confirm this: they still import from `runner_helpers` and the tests were updated accordingly.

### 2. `batches.py` (812 lines -> 465 lines)

**Where did the code go?** Split into two new files:

| New file | Lines | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `batches_scope.py` (262 lines) | Dimension scope/coverage helpers: `validate_runner`, `require_batches`, `print_review_quality`, `collect_reviewed_files_from_batches`, `normalize_dimension_list`, `scored_dimensions_for_lang`, `print_preflight_dimension_scope_notice`, `print_import_dimension_coverage_notice` |
| `batches_runtime.py` (379 lines) | Runtime execution infrastructure: `BatchProgressTracker`, `BatchRunSummaryConfig`, `build_batch_tasks`, `make_run_log_writer`, `resolve_run_log_path`, `write_run_summary` |

**Total new: 641 lines.** The remaining `batches.py` (465 lines) imports from these two modules with underscore-prefixed aliases and introduces:
- A `BatchRunDeps` dataclass that bundles the 17 callback/runtime parameters that `do_run_batches` previously accepted as keyword arguments
- A `_merge_and_import_batch_results` helper that consolidates the post-execution merge+import+coverage-reporting block that was inline in `do_run_batches`

**Verdict:** Good extraction. The scope/runtime split makes conceptual sense. The `BatchRunDeps` dataclass replacing 17 keyword arguments is a meaningful improvement to the call signature. No functionality deleted.

### 3. `batch_core.py` (753 lines -> 441 lines)

**Where did the code go?** The merge logic was extracted to:

| New file | Lines | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_merge.py` (297 lines) | All batch-result merge logic: `assessment_weight`, `merge_batch_results`, plus all the private accumulation/dedup helpers (`_accumulate_batch_scores`, `_finding_identity_key`, `_merge_finding_payload`, `_should_merge_findings`, `_accumulate_batch_findings`, `_accumulate_batch_quality`, `_compute_merged_assessments`, `_compute_abstraction_components`, `_finding_pressure_by_dimension`) |

**Additional change:** The legacy `LEGACY_DIMENSION_NOTE_ISSUES_KEY` fallback was dropped in `_validate_dimension_note`. The test was updated to confirm this intentional behavior change (test renamed from `test_normalize_batch_result_accepts_legacy_unreported_risk_key` to `test_normalize_batch_result_ignores_legacy_unreported_risk_key`). Similarly, the `LEGACY_REVIEW_QUALITY_HIGH_SCORE_MISSING_ISSUES_KEY` fallback was dropped from `_accumulate_batch_quality` in `batch_merge.py` and from `_print_review_quality` in `batches_scope.py`.

**Verdict:** Clean extraction. The merge logic belongs in its own module -- it's a self-contained algorithm. The legacy key removal is an intentional deprecation, not a bug.

### 4. Other modified files

**`runtime_paths.py` (61 lines, new):** Consolidates path-resolution logic that was duplicated across `batch.py`, `external.py`, and `import_helpers.py`. Each had its own `_runtime_project_root()`, `_review_packet_dir()`, `_blind_packet_path()`, etc. Now there's one source of truth with clean `*_override` parameters for test injection.

**`batch.py` (432 -> 523 lines, grew):** Introduced two new dataclasses:
- `ReviewBatchRuntimePaths` -- replaces the module-level mutable globals (`PROJECT_ROOT`, `REVIEW_PACKET_DIR`, `SUBAGENT_RUNS_DIR`) that tests patched. Now tests pass an explicit dataclass.
- `_BatchRunnerWiring` -- groups the method-creation logic that was previously done with inline lambdas in `_do_run_batches`. This is a clear improvement: the old code had deeply-nested lambdas that were hard to follow.

**`entrypoint.py` (212 -> 253 lines, grew):** Introduced `ReviewModeArgs` dataclass and `_parse_review_mode_args()` replacing the old `_mode_flags()` tuple return. The scattered `getattr(args, ...)` calls throughout `_run_review_mode` are now clean field accesses on a typed dataclass. This is a straightforward improvement.

**`external.py` (554 -> 553 lines, essentially unchanged in size):** Introduced `ExternalSubmitRequest` dataclass to replace the 10 keyword arguments to `do_external_submit`. Uses `runtime_paths.py` instead of local path-resolution functions. The module-level `PROJECT_ROOT`/`REVIEW_PACKET_DIR`/`EXTERNAL_SESSION_ROOT` globals are still present (they're still used by `do_external_start`), but the path-resolution functions are now in `runtime_paths.py`.

**`import_helpers.py`:** Switched from direct `get_project_root()` to the new `runtime_paths` module. Small, clean change.

**`prepare.py`:** Added type annotations to `do_prepare` signature. Trivial improvement.

### 5. Are there broken references?

**No critical breaks found.** The analysis shows:

- `runner_helpers.py` re-exports everything that external code imports. All test files that `import runner_helpers` will continue to work.
- The old module-level globals (`batch.PROJECT_ROOT`, `batch.REVIEW_PACKET_DIR`, `batch.SUBAGENT_RUNS_DIR`) have been removed, and all test patches have been updated to pass `ReviewBatchRuntimePaths` instead. No leftover references to the old globals were found in the codebase.
- `external.py` still has its own `PROJECT_ROOT`/`REVIEW_PACKET_DIR`/`EXTERNAL_SESSION_ROOT` module-level globals (line references in its current code), which is slightly inconsistent -- those are used only by `do_external_start` and `_session_dir`. The `do_external_submit` path has been cleaned up but the start path still uses the old globals. This is a minor inconsistency but not a breakage.

### 6. Summary assessment

**This is a well-executed decomposition of oversized modules, not a deletion of functionality.** The key metrics:

| Module | Before (lines) | After (lines) | New files (lines) | Total after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runner_helpers.py` | 1,512 | 310 (facade) | 1,461 | 1,771 |
| `batches.py` | 812 | 465 | 641 | 1,106 |
| `batch_core.py` | 753 | 441 | 297 | 738 |
| `batch.py` | 432 | 523 | -- | 523 |
| `entrypoint.py` | 212 | 253 | -- | 253 |
| `external.py` | 554 | 553 | -- | 553 |
| `runtime_paths.py` | -- | -- | 61 | 61 |

Total lines went up, not down, which confirms this is restructuring, not deletion.

**What improved:**
- **Single-responsibility:** Each new file has a clear, narrow purpose (failures, packets, parallel execution, subprocess management, merge logic, scope checking, runtime tracking, path resolution).
- **Testability:** Module-level mutable globals replaced with explicit dataclass parameters (`ReviewBatchRuntimePaths`, `BatchRunDeps`, `ExternalSubmitRequest`). No more `patch("module.PROJECT_ROOT")` -- tests pass data explicitly.
- **Readability:** The 17-parameter `do_run_batches` call is replaced with a single `deps: BatchRunDeps` dataclass. Inline lambda forests in `_do_run_batches` are replaced with named methods on `_BatchRunnerWiring`.
- **Backwards compatibility:** `runner_helpers.py` acts as a facade, so nothing breaks.

**Minor concerns:**
1. `external.py` still has module-level `PROJECT_ROOT`/`REVIEW_PACKET_DIR`/`EXTERNAL_SESSION_ROOT` globals for the `do_external_start` path, while `do_external_submit` was moved to the new dataclass pattern. This asymmetry should be cleaned up in a follow-up.
2. The `BatchRunDeps` dataclass uses `object` for all its callback fields rather than proper `Callable` types. This makes IDE support and static analysis weaker than it could be. `batches_runtime.py` does use `Callable` properly for similar fields, so the inconsistency is notable.
3. The legacy key removal (`LEGACY_DIMENSION_NOTE_ISSUES_KEY`, `LEGACY_REVIEW_QUALITY_HIGH_SCORE_MISSING_ISSUES_KEY`) is a behavioral change bundled into a structural refactor. This should ideally be a separate commit for clarity.
4. `batches.py` imports from `batches_scope` with underscore-aliased names (e.g., `collect_reviewed_files_from_batches as _collect_reviewed_files_from_batches`), which is a bit unusual -- it uses private-looking names internally but they're just re-imported public functions. This is a style choice, not a bug.

**Overall:** This is a solid refactoring. The extraction boundaries are logical, the facade pattern preserves backwards compatibility, and the dataclass replacements for mutable globals and long parameter lists are genuine improvements.

## Assessment of Engine, Scoring, and Intelligence Layer Changes

### 1. Large Deletions: Are They Losing Functionality?

**`intelligence/review/dimensions/metadata.py` (-258 lines):** No functionality lost. The entire body was moved verbatim to the new file `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/core/subjective_dimensions.py`. The old module becomes a thin re-export shim -- all 8 public names (`default_display_names_map`, `dimension_display_name`, `dimension_weight`, `get_dimension_metadata`, `load_subjective_dimension_metadata`, `load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang`, `resettable_default_dimensions`) are re-exported from the new location, and the `__all__` list is preserved. This is a clean, no-loss relocation.

**`app/output/scorecard_parts/dimensions.py` (-210 lines):** No functionality lost. All functions (`resolve_scorecard_lang`, `is_unassessed_subjective_placeholder`, `collapse_elegance_dimensions`, `limit_scorecard_dimensions`, `prepare_scorecard_dimensions`) were moved to `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/planning/dimension_rows.py`. The old module becomes a re-export shim with the same `__all__`.

**`app/output/scorecard_parts/dimension_policy.py` (-89 lines):** Constants and the `_compose_scorecard_dimensions` helper moved to the new file `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/planning/scorecard_policy.py`. The old module re-exports everything. No loss.

**Verdict:** All three large deletions are pure relocations to lower-layer modules. The old modules are preserved as re-export shims so no downstream imports break.

### 2. `dimension_rows.py` Expansion (+194 net lines) -- Design Quality

The expansion is well-designed. It absorbs the functions previously in `app/output/scorecard_parts/dimensions.py`, moving them from the app layer down to the engine/planning layer. This is architecturally correct because:

- **Eliminates a layering violation.** Previously, `scorecard_dimension_rows()` in the engine layer had to do a deferred `try: from desloppify.app.output.scorecard_parts.dimensions import prepare_scorecard_dimensions` -- an engine module reaching up into the app layer. Now the logic lives natively in the engine and the app module re-exports downward, which is the proper dependency direction.
- **The code is a byte-for-byte copy** of the original functions with no logic changes. I compared `collapse_elegance_dimensions`, `limit_scorecard_dimensions`, `prepare_scorecard_dimensions`, `resolve_scorecard_lang`, and `is_unassessed_subjective_placeholder` -- all are identical to their former locations.
- **The fallback path in `scorecard_dimension_rows`** is simplified: the `try/except ImportError` wrapper around the deferred import is removed since the function is now local. The fallback still exists for synthetic/test states.

### 3. Engine Changes -- Clean Refactors vs. Behavior Changes

**Pure refactors (no behavior change):**

- **`_plan/persistence.py`:** Extracts inline validation into a reusable `_coerce_plan_model()` helper that raises `PlanLoadError` instead of returning `empty_plan()` directly. The caller still catches `PlanLoadError` and falls back to `empty_plan()`. Net behavior identical.
- **`_scoring/subjective/core.py`:** `DISPLAY_NAMES` dict and the helper functions `_dimension_display_name`/`_dimension_weight` are replaced with direct imports from `core.subjective_dimensions`. The deferred `try/except ImportError` wrappers are removed. This is safe because the circular dependency that motivated them has been broken -- `core.subjective_dimensions` only imports from `core._internal.text_utils` (no engine or intelligence imports at module level; it uses deferred imports for dimension data loading).
- **`_state/scoring.py`:** Same pattern -- moves `from desloppify.scoring import ...` to module level (from a deferred import inside `_update_objective_health`), and replaces the deferred `load_dimensions_for_lang` import with `default_dimension_keys_for_lang` from `core.subjective_dimensions`. Safe for the same reason.
- **`detectors/coverage/mapping.py`, `detectors/review_coverage.py`, `detectors/test_coverage/heuristics.py`:** Import path change from `desloppify.hook_registry` to `desloppify.engine.hook_registry`. The old top-level `hook_registry.py` is being deleted (`D desloppify/hook_registry.py` in git status) and the new location is `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/hook_registry.py` -- identical content. Clean relocation.
- **`_work_queue/core.py`:** Adds `logging` import and replaces `_ = exc` with `logger.debug(...)`. No behavior change.
- **`_work_queue/helpers.py` `is_subjective_finding`:** Simplifies an if/elif chain to a single `in` check. Equivalent logic.

**Actual behavior changes:**

1. **`_work_queue/helpers.py` `primary_command_for_finding` -- BUG FIX (important):**
   - Old: `if supported_fixers is not None and fixer in supported_fixers`
   - New: `if supported_fixers is None or fixer in supported_fixers`
   - The old code was inverted. When `supported_fixers=None` (meaning "all fixers are available"), the old condition evaluated to `False` for every fixer, meaning the auto-fix command path was **never reached** when no filter was provided. The fix is correct: `None` means "no filter, accept all."

2. **`_work_queue/helpers.py` `build_subjective_items` -- dead branch removal:**
   - Two `elif` branches for `is_stale` and `cli_keys` (non-unassessed, non-open-review) are removed. Both called `_prepare_command(cli_keys, force_review_rerun=True)`. The remaining `else` branch also calls `_prepare_command(cli_keys, force_review_rerun=True)`. So all three branches were producing the same output -- the removal is correct deduplication.

3. **`_scoring/policy/core.py` -- dimension remap:**
   - `subjective_review` detector moved from dimension `"Test health"` to `"Code quality"`.
   - This is a deliberate semantic correction, not an accident. The comment says "Subjective review freshness/coverage is a code-quality maintenance signal, not a direct test-quality signal." This will change where subjective_review findings contribute in the scorecard.

4. **`core/registry.py` -- detector dimension remap:**
   - Both `"review"` and `"subjective_review"` detectors changed from `"Test health"` to `"Design coherence"`. This is consistent with the scoring policy change above -- design review findings belong in a design dimension, not test health.

5. **`core/exception_sets.py` -- tightened exception handling:**
   - `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` reduced from `(ImportError, AttributeError, OSError, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError)` to `(PlanLoadError, OSError)`. This is intentionally stricter -- programming errors like `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `KeyError` will no longer be silently swallowed during plan loading. Instead, only explicit `PlanLoadError` (raised by the new `_coerce_plan_model`) and `OSError` (filesystem failures) are recoverable. This is a good change that will surface real bugs faster.

### 4. Core Layer Changes

**`core/_internal/text_utils.py` -- `_LazyProjectRoot`:** Replaces the eagerly-evaluated `PROJECT_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_ROOT", Path.cwd())).resolve()` with a lazy proxy object. This fixes a subtle bug where `PROJECT_ROOT` captured `cwd()` at import time, which could be wrong if the working directory changed before the module was first used. The proxy delegates to `Path` via `__fspath__`, `__truediv__`, `__getattr__`, etc. The `get_project_root()` function is updated to handle the proxy type.

**`core/paths_api.py` -- sentinel removal:** The old code used identity comparisons (`PROJECT_ROOT is not _PROJECT_ROOT_SENTINEL`) to detect overrides, which is fragile. The new code initializes `PROJECT_ROOT = None` (instead of a sentinel Path) and uses `_coerce_path_override()` to check for non-None Path/str values. Cleaner and more robust.

**`core/skill_docs.py`:** Replaces `_ = exc` with `logger.debug(...)`. Minor improvement.

### 5. Intelligence/Review Layer

**`context_holistic/mechanical.py` (+42 lines for `_DetectorFinding` dataclass + `_extract_findings_by_detector`):** This is a well-designed DRY refactor. Every builder function (`_build_boundary_violations`, `_build_dead_code`, `_build_private_crossings`, `_build_duplicate_clusters`, `_build_flat_dir_findings`, `_build_security_hotspots`) previously duplicated the same boilerplate pattern:
```python
for finding in by_detector.get("detector_name", []):
    filepath = finding.get("file", "")
    detail = finding.get("detail", {})
    if not isinstance(detail, dict):
        detail = {}
```
The new `_extract_findings_by_detector` centralizes this, and the `_DetectorFinding` frozen dataclass gives typed access to `.detector`, `.finding`, `.file`, `.detail`. No logic change -- pure extraction.

**Type annotations (`prepare.py`, `prepare_batches.py`, `orchestrator.py`, `selection.py`):** Replace `lang: object` with `lang: LangRuntimeContract` behind `TYPE_CHECKING` guards. No runtime effect, but improves IDE support and type checking.

**`feedback_contract.py` -- `HIGH_SCORE_UNREPORTED_RISK_THRESHOLD` alias removal:** The backward-compatibility alias is deleted. Grep confirms zero remaining consumers across the codebase. Safe removal.

**`detectors/flat_dirs.py` -- `FlatDirConfig` dataclass:** Replaces 12 individual keyword parameters with a frozen dataclass. The old API is preserved via `**legacy_overrides` that get mapped onto the dataclass. The `_resolve_flat_dir_config` helper validates unknown keys and normalizes `thin_wrapper_names` from list to tuple. This is a clean interface improvement that retains backward compatibility.

### 6. Red Flags

**One concern with `_LazyProjectRoot`:** The `__getattr__` proxy delegates all attribute access to `self._resolve()`, which returns a fresh `Path` on each call. This means `PROJECT_ROOT.resolve()`, `PROJECT_ROOT.parent`, etc. all work, but each call re-evaluates `Path(os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_ROOT", Path.cwd())).resolve()`. If `cwd()` changes between calls and `DESLOPPIFY_ROOT` is not set, the root will silently shift. Whether this is a feature or a bug depends on intent. If the goal is "lazily capture once," a `lru_cache` or a `_cached` attribute would be safer. If the goal is "always reflect current state," this is correct. Given that `get_project_root()` (the preferred API) also calls `_resolve()` without caching, this appears intentional -- but it is a semantic change from the old behavior where `PROJECT_ROOT` was stable once captured.

**Minor style nit in `_work_queue/core.py`:** The `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` line is placed between two import blocks rather than after all imports. This is cosmetic only and won't cause issues, but it violates typical Python style convention.

**The detector dimension remaps are behavior changes that will affect scoring.** Moving `review` and `subjective_review` from "Test health" to "Design coherence" / "Code quality" will redistribute scores across dimensions for any existing scan state. This is intentional but worth noting -- existing users may see scorecard shifts after upgrading.

### Summary

Overall, this is a well-executed architectural cleanup with three main themes:

1. **Dependency direction repair** -- moving shared data (dimension metadata, scorecard policy, hook registry) from higher layers (app, intelligence) down to lower layers (core, engine) so that engine modules no longer need deferred imports or `try/except ImportError` hacks to reach upward.

2. **DRY extraction** -- `_DetectorFinding` in mechanical.py, `FlatDirConfig` in flat_dirs.py, `_coerce_plan_model` in persistence.py.

3. **One genuine bug fix** -- the inverted `supported_fixers` condition in `primary_command_for_finding` that was preventing auto-fix commands from being suggested.

The changes are clean. No functionality is lost in the large deletions. The re-export shims preserve backward compatibility. The tightened exception set in `PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS` is the only change that could surface new exceptions in production, but that is deliberately trading silent corruption for explicit failure, which is the right tradeoff.

   430→        "run_stamp": str(session.get("session_id", "")),
   431→        "created_at": _iso_seconds(_utc_now()),
   432→        "packet_path": str(session.get("blind_packet_path", "")),
   433→        "packet_sha256": str(session.get("packet_sha256", "")),
   434→        "external_session_id": expected_id,
   435→    }
   436→    return payload
   437→
   438→
   439→def _ensure_session_open_or_exit(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   440→    status = str(session.get("status", "open")).strip().lower()
   441→    if status == "open":
   442→        return
   443→    print(
   444→        colorize(
   445→            f"  Error: session is not open (status={status or 'unknown'}). Start a new session with --external-start.",
   446→            "red",
   447→        ),
   448→        file=sys.stderr,
   449→    )
   450→    sys.exit(1)
   451→
   452→
   453→def _ensure_session_not_expired_or_exit(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   454→    expires_at = _parse_iso(session.get("expires_at"))
   455→    if expires_at is None:
   456→        print(
   457→            colorize(
   458→                "  Error: session metadata is missing/invalid expires_at.",
   459→                "red",
   460→            ),
   461→            file=sys.stderr,
   462→        )
   463→        sys.exit(1)
   464→    now = _utc_now()
   465→    if now <= expires_at:
   466→        return
   467→    print(
   468→        colorize(
   469→            f"  Error: session expired at {session.get('expires_at')}. Start a new session with --external-start.",
   470→            "red",
   471→        ),
   472→        file=sys.stderr,
   473→    )
   474→    sys.exit(1)
   475→
   476→
   477→def do_external_submit(request: ExternalSubmitRequest) -> None:
   478→    """Submit external reviewer output via session, adding canonical provenance."""
   479→    config = request.config or {}
   480→    session_path, session = _session_payload_or_exit(request.session_id)
   481→    _ensure_session_open_or_exit(session)
   482→    _ensure_session_not_expired_or_exit(session)
   483→
   484→    if str(session.get("runner", "")).strip().lower() not in _EXTERNAL_SUPPORTED_RUNNERS:
   485→        print(
   486→            colorize(
   487→                "  Error: only Claude external sessions currently support durable score submit.",
   488→                "red",
   489→            ),
   490→            file=sys.stderr,
   491→        )
   492→        sys.exit(1)
   493→
   494→    findings_path = Path(request.import_file)
   495→    raw_payload = _load_json_object(findings_path, label="external findings")
   496→    canonical_payload = _canonical_external_payload(raw_payload, session=session)
   497→
   498→    stamp = runner_helpers_mod.run_stamp()
   499→    session_dir = session_path.parent
   500→    canonical_path = session_dir / f"canonical_import_{stamp}.json"
   501→    safe_write_text(canonical_path, json.dumps(canonical_payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   502→
   503→    if request.dry_run:
   504→        do_validate_import(
   505→            str(canonical_path),
   506→            request.lang,
   507→            allow_partial=request.allow_partial,
   508→            attested_external=True,
   509→            manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   510→        )
   511→        return
   512→
   513→    do_import(
   514→        str(canonical_path),
   515→        request.state,
   516→        request.lang,
   517→        request.state_file,
   518→        config=config,
   519→        allow_partial=request.allow_partial,
   520→        attested_external=True,
   521→        manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   522→    )
   523→
   524→    submitted_at = _iso_seconds(_utc_now())
   525→    session["status"] = "submitted"
   526→    session["submitted_at"] = submitted_at
   527→    session["submitted_input_file"] = str(findings_path)
   528→    session["submitted_canonical_file"] = str(canonical_path)
   529→    safe_write_text(session_path, json.dumps(session, indent=2) + "\n")
   530→
   531→    if request.scan_after_import:
   532→        code = runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   533→            lang_name=request.lang.name,
   534→            scan_path=request.scan_path,
   535→            deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   536→                project_root=runtime_project_root(project_root_override=PROJECT_ROOT),
   537→                timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   538→                python_executable=sys.executable,
   539→                subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   540→                timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   541→                colorize_fn=colorize,
   542→            ),
   543→        )
   544→        if code != 0:
   545→            raise SystemExit(code)
   546→
   547→
   548→__all__ = [
   549→    "EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT",
   550→    "ExternalSubmitRequest",
   551→    "do_external_start",
   552→    "do_external_submit",
   553→]
